pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 3.1.1 LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we describe objects?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. recognise adjectives (colour, shape, siz
2. use adjectives correctly in conversations related to the theme for effective communication
3. enjoy using adjectives to make inferences in varied communication contexts

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension

Teach
• Focus skill: recognise adjectives (colour, shape, siz.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we describe objects?
2. How can we assist those affected during a disaster?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
